clue.text: Canto I could be unstressed

indicators.note: 'could be' says the letters before it might become something else once rearranged

parts.note: the six letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark on verse: the first canto of a poem might be read without emphasis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canto I' reads as a poem's first section, but it is just six letters to rearrange into ATONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonic is the phonetics term for a syllable carrying no accent, so it means unstressed.

clue.text: I go into Scarlett's place for this ornamental headgear

indicators.note: to go into something is to enter it, so the letter sits inside the place

parts.note: Tara is Scarlett O'Hara's plantation home in Gone with the Wind
taken as written

explanation.surface: A visitor to Scarlett O'Hara's estate looking for a jewelled headdress.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head, a decorative kind of headgear.

clue.text: The nostrils are between the poles

indicators.note: 'between' puts the verb in the middle, flanked by the two ends of the earth

parts.note: N and S, north and south, are the two poles
taken as written

explanation.surface: A geography-meets-anatomy statement that the nose lies between two poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Nares is the Latin-derived anatomical term for the nostrils, the openings of the nose.

clue.text: Came round Park with coniferous tree to find billy-boiler

indicators.note: 'round' means the first word surrounds what follows it

parts.note: taken as written
P is the road-sign abbreviation for park or parking
the fir is a conifer

explanation.surface: A walker comes round a park with fir trees, searching for a spot to brew tea.
explanation.walkthrough: A billy is the Australian tin can used for boiling water over an open fire, so this is an Australian definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Australian bush a billy of tea is heated over a campfire, so the fire is what boils the billy.

clue.text: Border upon turning a wind instrument

indicators.note: turning something about makes it face the other way, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: the tuba is a large brass wind instrument

explanation.surface: A band at the frontier, an instrument turning at the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to share a boundary with, to lie directly against or border upon.

clue.text: Parts of hands holding old shilling for sacred songs

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so the coin goes within the hands

parts.note: the palm is the inner part of the hand
s was the abbreviation for the shilling in old British and Australian money

explanation.surface: Hands holding out a coin for the church collection during hymns.
explanation.definitionFit: The Psalms are the sacred songs of the Old Testament, and psalms are sung in worship.

clue.text: Salad item to get mother to finish

parts.note: taken as written
ma is a familiar name for mother
a second 'to', placed at the end

explanation.surface: A child asking mum to finish the salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To finish' means the second 'to' comes last: TO + MA + TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomato is a staple raw ingredient of a green salad, so it is a salad item.

clue.text: Boss eats enough to become fireproof

indicators.note: the words before have just enough letters to become something new when they are reordered

parts.note: eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: The boss eats so much that he becomes impervious to fire, like a fire-eater.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'eats' a verb, but 'Boss eats' simply supplies the eight letters of ASBESTOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is the mineral fibre once used for fire-resistant materials, so as a noun used attributively it stands for fireproof.

clue.text: Howl with some spirit for this perfume

parts.note: to bay is to howl, as a hound does
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: A spooky picture: a howl mixed with a ghost to make a scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests a ghost to go with the howl; here it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay rum is an aromatic lotion made from bay leaves and rum, used as a cologne or aftershave.

clue.text: Kneecaps for tall apes, perhaps

indicators.note: 'perhaps' hints the letters are one possible arrangement among others

parts.note: eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Protective knee pads for lanky gorillas.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the anatomical name for the kneecap bone, so patellas are kneecaps.

clue.text: See this mountain range, if following church service

indicators.note: 'following' tells us the conditional word comes after the service in the answer

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic eucharistic service
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to view the mountains, provided you have been to church first.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains forming a single block, a kind of range.

clue.text: Disturbed foreman in 8 bursts into tears

indicators.note: something disturbed is thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: clue 8 begins with the word Boss, a foreman

explanation.surface: An upset foreman in the asbestos trade breaks down crying.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to the word Boss in the clue for 8 across, a synonym for foreman.
explanation.definitionFit: To sob is to weep noisily, so sobs is to cry, one who bursts into tears.

clue.text: Tax alternative for a swindler?

parts.note: an impost is a tax or duty
'or' is the word that introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Asks whether a tax-avoidance scheme is really a con man's alternative to paying.
explanation.definitionFit: An impostor deceives people by pretending to be someone else, a kind of swindler or cheat.

clue.text: Excellent examples of glib talk to bridge partners

parts.note: patter is quick, smooth sales talk
North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Smooth chatter offered as model behaviour to card players at the bridge table.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge the four players are North, South, East and West; N and S play as a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern can be a model worth copying, an exemplar, so patterns are excellent examples.

clue.text: Final resting place to a doctor

parts.note: taken as written
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A grim joke that seeing the doctor leads to the grave.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomb is a burial chamber or grave, where a body is laid for good.

clue.text: Sailor's back, sent to take me in. It's a low story

indicators.note: 'back' asks for the sailor's abbreviation to be read in the opposite direction

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

indicators.note: 'to take ... in' means to enclose, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; goes inside the previous piece

explanation.surface: A sailor returns, sent to collect someone, followed by a story told at a low level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story' looks like a tale to be told, but it is the American spelling of storey, a floor of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A basement is the floor of a building below ground level, the lowest storey.

clue.text: Before noon alphabet extremes are on this river

parts.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before midday
A and Z are the first and last letters of the alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A morning scene: travellers on a river from start to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon is the great South American river, the largest in the world by flow.

clue.text: Endear, perhaps. It could be merited

indicators.note: 'perhaps' suggests the word is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: six letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Musing that winning affection may be something deserved.
explanation.definitionFit: Earned and merited both describe something gained through deserving it.

clue.text: Turn round a degree for this headgear

indicators.note: 'round' means the first word wraps itself around the degree

parts.note: taken as written
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A graduate turning in a circle to show off a mortarboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn round' reads as one phrase meaning rotate; split it, and 'round' puts the degree inside TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: A turban is a long cloth wound round the head, a traditional form of headgear.

clue.text: Dance rhythm in some bongo-drum band

indicators.note: 'some' of a phrase means just a part of it, the letters found inside

parts.note: the letters run across the end of drum and the start of band

explanation.surface: Describes a band of bongo drummers playing a Latin beat.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban dance, and its name also covers the music and beat it is danced to.

clue.text: Nears a change for TV's Lou Grant

indicators.note: a change of order rearranges the letters of the word before

parts.note: five letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A TV newsroom character approaches a turning point in his storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: Lou Grant was the gruff newsman in The Mary Tyler Moore Show and its spin-off Lou Grant.
explanation.definitionFit: Actor Ed Asner played the character Lou Grant on American television, so the surname stands for the role.

clue.text: Means of transport to care about ruined Latvian city

indicators.note: 'about' means the first word goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something ruined is broken apart, so the city's letters are jumbled

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: A transport service in a war-damaged Baltic city.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled city does not go in the middle of the enclosing word but just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A carriage is a wheeled vehicle, horse-drawn or a railway coach, so it is a way of travelling.

clue.text: I'm entering as objectives

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so it sits within the following word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone announcing their arrival in a role as the goals of a project.
explanation.definitionFit: Aims are the goals one sets out to reach, the same thing as objectives.

clue.text: No army could upset this gipsy

indicators.note: upsetting something knocks it over and disorders it, so the letters change places

parts.note: six letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A lone traveller so formidable that no army could trouble them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romany are a travelling people traditionally called gipsies, and the word also names a member of that people.

clue.text: Roman bed designed for a big dog

indicators.note: something designed is newly made up, so the letters are put into a new form

parts.note: eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A grand classical couch built for a large pet hound.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dobermann is a large German guard-dog breed, so it is an example of a big dog.

clue.text: Arrived briefly in pig house — quite stellar

indicators.note: 'in' places the shortened word inside the animal's dwelling

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
ARR is the timetable abbreviation for arrived

explanation.surface: Someone turns up at a pigsty, and the result is somehow dazzling.
explanation.definitionFit: Starry means full of or like stars, which is what stellar describes.
